## 3. Abstract Dynamic Programs

This section is a brief review of the dynamic programming framework from Sargent and Stachurski (2025). We repeat the key definitions to make the paper partly selfcontained.

3.1. Definition and Properties. An abstract dynamic program (ADP) is a pair ( V, ❚ ), where

- (i) V = ( V, ⪯ ) is a poset and
- (ii) ❚ = { T σ : σ ∈ Σ } is a nonempty family of order preserving self-maps on V .

We call V the value space . Each operator T σ in ❚ is called a policy operator . Σ is an arbitrary index set and elements of Σ are called policies . In applications, we impose conditions under which each T σ has a unique fixed point. In these settings, the significance of each policy operator T σ is that its fixed point, denoted below by v σ , represents the lifetime value of following policy σ .
